title: The NF-05 legacy story text is absent, and the gate thresholds, the tool products, the exception expiry and the reporting surface are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R7.3 and R9; _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json NF-05 entry (title only, every other field empty); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 29, 35, 38 and 47; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 NFR-052 and NFR-054; ownership.json (no gate set, no threshold, no gate product, no exception value, no release report)
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 16 Test cases; 19 Out of scope
description: No source read gives the NF-05 legacy story text, so the baseline has no legacy acceptance criterion, legacy test case or legacy requirement to inherit and is derived from the named architecture slides. No source read gives the coverage floor of the unit and component gate, the duplication limit, the severity cut-off of static analysis, the tool product behind each of the eight gates, the licence source of the dependency gate, the length of the time-boxed exception, the approver role of an exception, the set of gates marked non-waivable beyond the blocking gates of NFR-054, the expiry behaviour of an exception at the moment it lapses, or the name and form of the reporting surface the platform administrator reads.
evidence: The NF-05 row of the legacy index carries the title "Quality gates baseline" with meta, module, release, requirements, acceptance criteria, test cases, messages, sections, status and story file all empty; NFR-052 and NFR-054 give the rule and the target ("No secrets in code or prompts", "Pipeline checks pass") and no threshold; Arch v5 slide 11 gives contract tests in every build and no level or floor, slide 20 gives the service template and contract tests as its parts and no gate list, slide 29 gives the boundary test in every build and no coverage number, slide 35 gives 800-204C and 800-204D as the standards for the DevSecOps pipeline and no product, slide 38 gives the golden pipeline in wave 0 and no rule, and slide 47 gives the boundary test as a mitigation and no expiry; and the ownership map lists no gate set, no threshold and no release report.
proposed: Publish the coverage floor, the duplication limit and the severity cut-off, the tool product behind each of the eight gates and the licence source of the dependency gate, the length of the exception box with its approver role and its expiry behaviour, the set of gates marked non-waivable, and the name and form of the release report, at the wave 0 exit check with the DevOps lead, the security architect and the release manager; a value that is still open is carried as a value of the gate-set version so that closing it needs no code change and produces one new gate-set version.

title: The target module-map location, the front-end module layout and the per-service package map are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-TE-001 sections 4 (steps 2 and 4) and 13 (Package); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 sections R4 and R5.5 (DP-01)
description: No source read fixes three target values that this legacy key needs after the split into 19 services. (a) Module map location: the legacy story has one file architecture/recovery-modules.yaml for the monolith, and no source places that file in the service template or in a per-service repository. (b) Front-end module layout: the legacy story names src/modules/recovery and one dependency rule file, and no source gives the layout after the split, or says whether each service keeps its own front-end module or all screens stay in one front end. (c) Per-service package map: Template and Rules section R4 fixes the Java package pattern th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.<short without hyphen>, and no source enumerates the packages inside each repository, the position of the api and internal split, or how a published package of one module is named once the module is a service of its own.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-001 section 4 step 2 (one map file architecture/recovery-modules.yaml for the 19 modules), step 4 (src/modules/recovery) and section 13 (one package per module, each with api and internal; front end folder src/modules/recovery); Architecture v5 slides 20 (every service built from the service template and the shared libraries), 29 (19 Recovery schemas rwb_<service>, one login each, a boundary test in every build) and 41 (the 19 services); Template and Rules section R4 (package pattern) and section R5.5 DP-01; no slide, technical specification, service template document or module map names a repository layout, a module map path or a package map for a service repository.
proposed: Fix the module map path, the front-end module layout and the per-service package map in the Service Template Specification v1 at the wave 0 template review, before the first service repository is generated, and let every repository inherit them from the template.

title: The per-service module-map file name and the gateway-bff composite route list are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-TE-001 section 4 (step 2); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20 and 29; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 (DP-19)
description: Two values the delta needs are absent. (a) After the split each service repository keeps a module map of its own, and no source names that file, its directory or its scope, while the legacy map is one file for all 19 modules. (b) The boundary rule for screens points at the gateway-bff composite route, and no source gives the composite route list or its schema; the list belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the API Specification of gateway-bff, neither of which is in this work package, so the story can test the rule but cannot enumerate the routes.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-001 section 4 step 2 (one module map for the 19 modules) and section 13 (front end rules no import from src/modules/collection); Architecture v5 slides 11 (browser, then BFF, then owner; depth one only), 20 (gateway-bff composes at most a few parallel calls and never calls a service that then calls another) and 29 (boundary test in every build); Template and Rules section R5.5 DP-19 (gateway-bff composite route, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); no source names a per-service map file or lists the composite routes of gateway-bff.
proposed: Name the per-service module map in the Service Template Specification v1, and let RWB-PLT-N001-CON publish the gateway-bff composite route list; the template reads that list from the contract and adds no route of its own.

title: The target repository layout and the target branch ruleset of a service repository are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 002 Code owners for the recovery module v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 20 and 29
description: The preserved story fixes one code owners file and one branch rule for the one monolith repository. No source in the set states the target value for the folder set a code owner entry must cover in a service repository, or the branch ruleset that replaces the branch rule on main in each of the 19 service repositories and the platform repository; the target values are derived by RWB-PLT-TE002-OPS from the platform template and from DP-07, DP-15 and DP-19.
evidence: Legacy 12 gives 'File: .github/CODEOWNERS at the repository root' with seven monolith paths and 'Branch rule on main: Require a pull request; require review from code owners; 1 approval; dismiss stale approvals; the author's approval does not count'; no source in the set restates either value for a service repository.
proposed: Keep the as-built file and branch rule unchanged in RWB-PLT-TE002-APP, and derive the per-repository folder set and ruleset in RWB-PLT-TE002-OPS from the platform template and the three DPs, with the solution architect confirming both before the delta is marked Done.

title: The team handles, the ruleset name and the required-check list and its order are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB TE 002 Code owners for the recovery module v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 20, 29, 35 and 38
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 19 Out of scope
description: The delta needs one team handle for each of the 20 repositories, a ruleset name, and the required-check list with an order. The legacy story leaves team names to DL37 and names no ruleset; RWB-PLT-NF05-OPS and RWB-PLT-TE001-APP own the checks but no source in the set gives their check names or an order, so none of the three values can be copied from a source document.
evidence: Legacy 3: 'Names assumed until DL37 and DL36 are answered: @scb-ace/techx-recovery-tech-leads and @scb-ace/ace-team'; legacy 8 BR7: 'Team names are values in the file; a change of team is a change to the file, reviewed by both teams'; no source names a ruleset, a ruleset name or an ordered check list.
proposed: Use the as-built handle convention @scb-ace/<team-handle> with one handle per owning team, one ruleset per repository on the protected branch, and the required-check list as the quality gates of RWB-PLT-NF05-OPS followed by the module boundary test of RWB-PLT-TE001-APP, until the DevOps lead and the solution architect close the point.

title: Target API file layout, index format and per-service generated package names are not specified for the preserved contract-test story
source: WP B-PLT-TPL-02; legacy story RWB-TE-003 sections 3, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-13 and section R8.4 (API Specification split into 19 files plus gateway-bff and an index); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 13, 20 and 41
description: The as-built story fixes one file at api/recovery-api.yaml with base path /api/recovery/v1, one shared generated package and one front-end output folder. The target rule is one file per service, one for gateway-bff and an index, and the story must generate and test from its own service file. No source document gives the target file names and folder, the format of the index (what it lists, and whether it carries the release of an operation), or the generated package names a service uses once the shared generated package is gone. A build team therefore cannot name the files or the packages from the documents alone, and the delta story RWB-PLT-TE003-APP-2 has to state them as defaults.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-003 section 12 names api/recovery-api.yaml, the shared generated package from the module map and src/modules/recovery/api/generated; section 13 names <ACE base package>.recovery.generated.web, .generated.model and the contract test folder. Template and Rules v1 section R8.4 names 'API Specification split into 19 files plus gateway-bff and an index' without a file name or an index format; Arch v5 slides 11, 13, 20 and 41 fix the base path /api/recovery/<short>/v1 and one template per service but name no specification file or generated package
proposed: Fix the specification file names and folder, the index format and the generated package names in the platform template and in RWB-PLT-TE003-APP-2, and keep the as-built names only in the 'As built (monolith)' appendix of RWB-PLT-TE003-APP

title: Index location, gateway-bff x-module value and the report format across the 19 pipelines are not specified for the delta story
source: WP B-PLT-TPL-02; legacy story RWB-TE-003 sections 4, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 section R8.4 and section R5.5 DP-19; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 13, 20 and 41
description: The delta story splits the single file into 19 service files, one gateway-bff file and an index, and reports passed, failed and pending per service and per release. No source document gives the folder of the index, the x-module value that a gateway-bff operation carries (gateway-bff is shared platform and is not one of the 19 service shorts of section R4, so x-module P1 to P10 or S1 to S9 cannot describe it), or the shape of the aggregate report across 19 independent pipelines (one row per service and release, one row per operation, or a merged summary). The values used are defaults of the story and change no rule of its section 8.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-003 section 4 step 8 reports passed, failed and pending operations in one build; sections 12 and 13 fix one file and one report. Arch v5 slide 20 puts gateway-bff in the shared platform and not in the 19, so the x-module vocabulary of the API specification does not cover it; Arch v5 slides 11, 13 and 41 fix the base path and the one-hop rule but name no index file and no report format
proposed: Fix the index location and format, the x-module value for gateway-bff operations and the aggregate report columns in the platform template and in RWB-PLT-TE003-APP-2

title: The per-service staging schema, the per-service extract layout, the personal-data field registry operation and the tool schema are not defined for the 19-schema masked copy
source: RWB-TE-004 sections 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: RWB-TE-004 fixes one staging schema `recovery_next` for the single `recovery` schema, one tool table `masked_copy_load` in a tool schema `tools`, and a verifier that reads `sys_fields.is_personal` directly. Under Arch v5 slide 29 the load fills 19 schemas `rwb_<name>`, one login each, so four values are needed and no source has them: the staging schema name per service (the load needs one per service, and `<schema>_next` is only a convention), the layout of the extract per service (which file or file set carries which service's tables, and whether the manifest is per table or per service), the operation that returns the personal-data field list (the plan gives the field registry to RWB-P1-E1065-CON but no source names the operation and no path is invented), and the name of the schema that holds `masked_copy_load` when the 19 service schemas are the only schemas named in the architecture.
evidence: RWB-TE-004 section 13: 'the stage loads into schema `recovery_next` in SIT or UAT and renames it to `recovery` after the checks; ... a small table `masked_copy_load` in the tool's own schema `tools` records extract ID, environment, business date, masking rule version and result'. RWB-TE-004 section 3: 'the generator's personal data pattern checks and the sys_fields is_personal tags are available to the loader'. Architecture v5 slide 29: '19 RECOVERY SCHEMAS - ONE LOGIN EACH ... no cross-schema joins or keys'; slide 41 gives each service its schema and its first path and no platform or tool schema. The Ownership Map maps a table to a service code, never a table to a staging schema or a file of the extract.
proposed: Fix the staging suffix, the per-service extract layout, the field-registry operation and the tool schema name before the load is published, with the PII extract contract and the P1 source-data contract in the room; the working defaults recorded in ASM-B-PLT-TPL-02-TE004-1, ASM-B-PLT-TPL-02-TE004-2 and ASM-B-PLT-TPL-02-TE004-3 apply until then.
